title: English Podcast for Learning English | Make 2026 Your Best Year Yet | Daily Life English

sentences.t: Hello and welcome back to Leo English podcast.
We're very happy you're here with us today.
I'm Tina.
And I'm Leo.
On this channel, we help you speak English more naturally through real conversation.
We practice useful English for daily life, work, routines, feelings, and real communication.
Today's topic is positive, practical, and very timely.
We're talking about how to make 2026 your best year yet.
I like this topic because a new year always gives people fresh energy.
Yes, many people want better habits, better health, better time management, better relationships, and better English, too.
And sometimes people have big dreams, but they don't know how to talk about them in English.
Exactly. So, today we will practice simple, natural English for goals, routines, plans, motivation, and daily life improvement.
We'll share useful phrases, personal examples, small mistakes, practical tips, and real conversation practice.
If you enjoy learning with us, please like this video and subscribe to our channel.
And click the little bell, too, so you don't miss our next episode.
All right, let's get started.
Leo, how are you today?
I'm good, but I feel very thoughtful.
Thoughtful? Why?
Because a new year always makes me look at my life and ask hard questions.
Like what?
Like why do I buy snacks I don't need, and why do I sleep too late?
Those are very serious questions.
Thank you. I'm doing deep research on myself.
That sounds dangerous.
It is. The results are mixed.
I'm doing well today.
I feel calm and focused.
That sounds very Tina.
I take a slow morning, make coffee, write notes, and think about this year.
What do you think about?
I think about habits, goals, and what really matters in daily life.
Nice. What did you do this weekend?
On Saturday, I cleaned my apartment and organized my desk.
On Sunday, I meet a friend for lunch and talk about plans for the year.
That sounds productive.
What about you?
On Saturday, I make a list of goals, then I lose the list for 2 hours.
Very strong start.
Thank you. Then on Sunday, I find the list under a magazine and feel hopeful again.
That is a full emotional journey.
It really is.
Speaking of goals, fresh starts, and trying to live better, today's topic fits perfectly.
Yes, let's talk about how to make 2026 your best year yet in clear, simple English.
Let's start simple.
What does your best year yet mean?
I think it means a year where you grow, improve, and feel proud of your life.
Exactly. It does not mean a perfect year.
It means a better year.
I like that.
Better feels possible.
Perfect feels scary.
That is a very important point.
Many people make goals that are too big and too strict.
Yes, then they fail once and feel terrible.
Right. So, our first idea today is this.
A good year starts with realistic goals.
Wait, what does realistic mean?
Realistic means possible in real life.
Ah, so I study English 10 hours every day may not be realistic.
For most people, no.
But, I study English 20 minutes every day is more realistic.
That already sounds better.
Good. So, if someone wants a better year, the first question is, what do I really want?
Not what looks impressive, what actually matters.
Exactly. Some people want more rest, some want better health, some want stronger friendships, some want better money habits, some want better English.
I think many people try to change everything at once.
Yes, and that often creates stress.
So maybe 2026 becomes better if we choose a few important things, not 50 things.
I completely agree.
Let's talk about daily habits first.
Good idea. Habits shape the year.
Exactly. A year improves through daily life, not only big moments.
That sounds smart.
So if I sleep better, eat better, move more, and use my time better, the year changes slowly.
Yes, and notice the language we use.
We can say, "I want to build better habits."
Nice, or "I want a more balanced routine."
Very good. Another useful phrase is, "I want to be more consistent."
Wait, what does consistent mean?
It means doing something regularly, not only one time.
Ah, so if I exercise one day and then disappear for 2 weeks, that is not consistent.
That word is painful, but useful.
It is very useful.
A lot of people say, "I don't need a perfect plan, I need a consistent plan."
Wow, that is good.
Thank you. Now, let's get more specific.
What kind of daily habits help make a year better?
Sleep, exercise, food, money, reading, planning, and time with good people.
Excellent list. Let's take them one by one.
First, sleep.
Ah, yes, my old enemy.
You really need a better sleep routine, Leo.
I know. I sleep too late and then I feel tired all morning.
A useful sentence is, "I want to go to bed earlier this year.
Very simple.
Yes, or I want a healthier sleep schedule.
That sounds like a sentence many people need.
I think so, too.
Another one is, I feel better when I sleep well.
That is true for everyone, I think.
Probably, yes. Second, movement and exercise.
This one is always on goal lists.
Yes, because it affects energy, mood, and health.
A person can say, I want to move more in my daily life.
I like that because it sounds easier than, I become a fitness hero.
Exactly. Or, I want to walk more and sit less.
Nice, very real.
Third, food habits.
A dangerous, but important area.
Yes, people often say, I want to cook more at home, or I want to eat more balanced meals.
What does balanced mean here?
It means healthy in a reasonable way.
Not too much junk food, not too little nutrition.
Ah, okay. So, balanced meals help the body work well.
Exactly. Another useful phrase is, I want to be more mindful about what I eat.
Wait, what does mindful mean?
It means aware and thoughtful, not automatic.
So, if I eat chips while watching videos and don't even notice, that is not mindful.
I feel seen.
Good. Now, let's talk about time.
A big one.
Yes, many people want a better year, but they do not manage their time well.
They say yes to too many things, waste hours online, or avoid important tasks.
Exactly. So, a useful sentence is, I want to use my time more wisely.
I love that phrase.
Another one is, I want to waste less time on things that don't matter.
Very honest.
Yes, or I want to be more intentional with my day.
Hmm, what does intentional mean?
It means doing things with a clear purpose.
Ah, so not only reacting all day, actually choosing.
Exactly. That is a powerful idea.
I think many people live in reaction mode.
Very true. They answer messages, solve small problems, and reach night without energy.
That is me sometimes.
Many people feel that way.
A better year often starts with small planning.
Like writing down three important things for the day?
Exactly. Not 20 things, maybe three.
I like that because it feels possible.
Good. Now let's talk about money habits.
Another real-life topic.
Yes, a better year often includes better money choices.
People say, "I want to save more.
I want to spend less on things I don't need, or I want to track my spending."
Track means watch and record, right?
Yes, exactly.
So that is useful.
I think some people avoid money because it feels stressful.
That is true, but ignoring money usually makes stress bigger.
So a better year may include more honesty with money.
Exactly. Not fear, clarity.
I like that.
Not fear, clarity.
Good. Now let's move to relationships.
This part matters a lot.
It really does.
A better year is not only about productivity, it's also about people.
Yes, if your days are full, but your heart feels empty, something is wrong.
Beautifully said.
Thank you. I prepare one deep sentence for every episode.
I appreciate the effort.
Many people want to call family more, check in on friends more, or spend less time with draining people.
Wait, what does draining mean here?
It means people or situations that take too much energy from you.
Ah, yes. Everyone knows one draining person.
Probably. A useful sentence is, I want to protect my energy more this year.
That is a strong sentence.
Another one is, I want to spend more time with people who support me.
I really like that.
Or I want healthier boundaries.
Boundaries means limits, right?
Yes, clear limits in relationships and time.
So if I always say yes, but feel tired, I need better boundaries.
This is bigger than language, it's life.
It is, but talking about it in English helps learners express real thoughts.
True. We are not only teaching words, we are teaching life conversation.
Exactly. Now let's talk about English learning itself.
My favorite category.
Good. Many learners want 2026 to be the year they finally speak more.
Yes, not only study, but actually speak.
So useful sentences are, I want to speak English more confidently, I want to practice every day, and I want to stop being afraid of mistakes.
That last one is huge.
It is. Another one is, I want English to be part of my daily life.
Oh, that is so good.
Yes. That means listening while you cook, reading short things, speaking to yourself, sending voice notes, and practicing small conversations.
So English becomes normal, not only homework.
Exactly. That change matters a lot.
I think learners often ask, how do I improve fast?
But a better question is, how do I stay regular?
I completely agree.
Because fast improvement sounds exciting, but regular practice changes everything.
Very true. A better year often comes from small repeated actions.
Not one perfect week in January.
Exactly. That is a very important message.
Can we talk about goals versus systems?
Yes, definitely. A goal is the result you want.
A system is what you do regularly.
Ah, that is helpful.
For example, a goal is I want better English.
A system is I listen to English 20 minutes every day.
So, the system carries the goal.
Exactly. Another example, goal, I want better health.
System, I walk after dinner five times a week.
That makes things much clearer.
Good, because vague motivation disappears fast.
Daily systems stay.
What does vague mean?
It means not clear enough.
So, I want to be better is vague.
Yes, but I read 10 pages every night is clear.
That is such a good example.
Thank you. Let's talk about common mistakes people make at the start of a new year.
Oh, yes, the classic mistakes.
First, too many goals.
Yes, people want a new body, new career, new language, new apartment, new personality, and perfect skin by February.
Exactly. That is too much.
Second, goals without daily action.
Like wanting change but changing nothing.
Right. Third, quitting after one bad week.
That one hurts.
People think one messy week means the whole plan is dead.
Yes, but real growth is not perfectly straight.
I need that reminder.
Many people do.
Another mistake is comparing too much.
Comparing to friends, influencers, co-workers, or strangers online.
Yes, comparison can steal energy and focus.
So, maybe one good sentence is I want to focus on my own progress.
Excellent. That is a very healthy sentence.
What What motivation?
People always talk about motivation.
Motivation helps, but it isn't enough.
Yes, motivation changes.
Some days you feel strong, some days you feel lazy, tired, or distracted.
Oh, I know those days well.
That's why routine matters more than emotion.
So, a better year is not built only on excited feelings.
Exactly. It's built on small actions you repeat.
That is not flashy, but it is real.
Yes, real change is often quiet.
That is a beautiful sentence.
Thank you. Now, let's make this very practical.
Imagine a listener wants a better year.
What should they do first?
Choose two or three important areas.
Good, then?
Make one small habit for each area.
Excellent, then?
Put that habit into real daily life, not dream life.
Very good. Explain dream life.
Dream life is the version of me who wakes up at 5:00, drinks green juice, reads philosophy, and never wastes time.
And real life?
Real life is the version of me who needs coffee and honest plans.
Exactly. Habits should fit real life.
So, maybe instead of I study English 2 hours every morning, I say I study 15 minutes after dinner.
Perfect. That is realistic.
Another thing that helps is tracking progress.
Like checking boxes on a calendar?
Yes, or writing short notes.
I like visible progress.
It keeps me going.
Many people feel that way.
Another useful sentence is, I want to celebrate small wins.
Oh, I love that.
Small wins matter.
Reading five pages matters.
Taking one walk matters.
Saving a little money matters.
Speaking 1 minute of English matters.
That makes growth feel less scary.
Exactly. A better year does not come only from huge actions.
It comes from small things repeated well.
Can we do some mini examples of goal language?
Yes, let's do that.
First, health.
I want to sleep earlier and move more.
Good. Add a detail.
I go to bed by 11:00 and I walk after dinner.
Excellent. Next, money.
I want to spend less on random snacks and save more.
Very honest.
Painfully honest.
Next, relationships.
I want to call my parents every Sunday and reply to friends more regularly.
Great. Next, English.
I want English to be part of my daily routine, so I listen every morning.
Perfect. Next, time.
I want to use my phone less and read more at night.
Excellent. This kind of English feels very useful because it is about real life.
Exactly. That is why daily life English matters so much.
I think a better year also needs self-kindness.
Absolutely. If you speak to yourself badly all the time, progress feels heavy.
So, maybe another sentence is, I want to be more patient with myself.
Beautiful. Very important.
Or, I want to improve without punishing myself.
That is excellent, too.
Wow, this episode gets deep.
Sometimes real life English is deep.
True. Let's finish the main conversation with one final idea.
A better year is not a performance.
What do you mean?
I mean, it's not about looking successful for other people.
It's about building a life that feels healthier, calmer, and more meaningful for you.
That is such a strong message.
Thank you. So, 2026 becomes your best year not because it's perfect, but because you live it more intentionally.
There's that word again, intentionally.
Yes, with purpose, with thought, with care.
I like that very much.
You know, Leo, while we were talking, we used many useful words.
Yes, and they are all great for real daily life English.
Exactly. Let's review them one by one.
First word, realistic.
This means possible in real life.
A very important goal word.
Yes. In our conversation, we say good goals need to be realistic.
For example, I make a realistic study plan.
Another example is her goal is ambitious, but still realistic.
And a realistic habit is easier to keep.
So, realistic is better than impossible.
Exactly. Next word, consistent.
This means doing something regularly.
Another very important one.
Yes. For example, I try to be consistent with my sleep schedule.
Another example is he practices English in a consistent way.
And small consistent actions create change.
I like this word because it feels more useful than perfect.
Very good point.
Next word, balanced.
In this topic, balanced means healthy and reasonable.
Not too much and not too little.
Like balanced meals or a balanced routine.
Exactly. For example, I want a more balanced lifestyle.
Another example is she eats balanced meals during the week.
And a balanced day includes work and rest.
So, balance is not boring.
It is healthy.
Exactly. Next word, mindful.
This means aware and thoughtful.
I asked about this one earlier.
Yes, in our conversation we use it for food and daily choices.
For example, I try to be mindful about my spending.
Another example is he eats more mindfully now and a mindful choice is not automatic.
So mindful is the opposite of careless.
In many situations, yes, that is a helpful way to think about it.
Next word, intentional.
This means done with a clear purpose.
Another deep but useful word.
Yes. For example, I want to be more intentional with my time.
Another example is she lives in a more intentional way and an intentional routine supports your goals.
I like this word because it feels calm and focused.
Me, too. Next phrase, check in on.
This means contact someone to make sure they are okay.
Very useful for relationships.
Exactly. For example, I check in on my grandparents every week.
Another example is he checks in on his friend after a hard day and I want to check in on people more often this year.
That feels kind and real.
It does. Next word, boundaries.
This means limits you set to protect your time or energy.
Very important life word.
Yes. For example, I want healthier boundaries at work.
Another example is she sets boundaries with her time and good boundaries protect your energy.
So boundaries are not rude, they are healthy.
Exactly. Great point.
Next word, draining.
This means something takes too much energy from you.
We use that for people or situations.
Right. For example, long meetings are draining for me.
Another example is that friendship feels draining, and travel without rest is draining.
My personal connection is noisy places.
They are draining for me.
That makes sense.
Next word, vague.
This means not clear enough.
Ah, yes. Goal language needs this word.
Exactly. For example, my plan is too vague, so it doesn't help me.
Another example is a vague goal is hard to follow, and she changes her vague idea into a clear plan.
So, I want a better life is vague.
Yes, but I read 10 pages every night is clear.
Final phrase, small wins.
This means little successes that still matter.
I love this phrase.
Me, too. For example, I celebrate small wins during the week.
Another example is speaking 1 minute of English is a small win, and small wins help people stay motivated.
That phrase feels kind and encouraging.
Exactly. Now, let's do the quick summary list.
Good idea.
Realistic, possible in real life.
Consistent, doing something regularly.
Balanced, healthy and reasonable.
Mindful, aware and thoughtful.
Intentional, done with a clear purpose.
Check in on, contact someone to make sure they are okay.
Boundaries, limits that protect your time or energy.
Draining, taking too much energy from you.
Vague, not clear enough.
Small wins, little successes that still matter.
Okay, Leo. That was a lot of talking about making 2026 your best year yet.
Yes, I feel motivated, organized, and slightly exposed.
That sounds about right.
Let's think about what we learned.
Please organize my future, Tina.
First, we learned that your best year does not mean your perfect year.
It means a better, healthier, more meaningful year.
Right. Better feels possible.
Perfect feels exhausting.
Then we talked about realistic goals.
We said a good goal fits real life, not fantasy life.
And we learned that a few good goals are better than too many goals.
After that, we looked at habits and systems.
We talked about sleep, movement, food, time, money, relationships, and English practice.
Yes, and we used useful sentences like, "I want to be more consistent, I want to use my time more wisely,
and I want English to be part of my daily life."
Then we talked about relationships and energy.
We used phrases like, "I want to protect my energy, I want healthier boundaries, and I want to spend more time with supportive people."
That part matters a lot because a good year is not only about productivity.
Exactly. After that, we talked about common mistakes: too many goals, vague plans, quitting too fast, and comparing too much.
Yes, those mistakes make people lose hope early.
Finally, we talked about small wins and self-kindness.
A better year grows through repeated small actions, not one dramatic, perfect week.
So, the big message is simple.
A good year is built day by day.
Exactly. Clear goals, small habits, honest choices, and patience can change a lot.
And 2026 can become your best year if you live it with purpose.
Now, we want to hear from you.
This is our favorite part.
Yes, because your comments always help us make better videos.
Our question of the day is, what is one small habit you want to build in 2026?
I'll answer first.
I want to sleep earlier and use my phone less at night.
Why that one?
Because better sleep improves everything else for me.
That makes sense.
My answer is a little different.
I want to protect quiet time more carefully.
Nice. Why?
Because quiet time helps me think clearly and feel balanced.
See, we have different answers and that's okay.
Exactly. So, viewers, we want to know about you.
Please tell us in the comments.
You can write one small habit I want to build in 2026 is
or I want to improve blank because blank
or this year I want to be more blank.
You can keep it short.
One or two sentences are enough.
And if you want more practice, write three sentences about your goals for 2026.
Yes, that helps you practice real English and real life together.
Your comments help us make better videos and they also help you practice writing.
So, don't be shy.
We really want to hear from you.
Thank you so much for learning with us today.
We're really glad you spent this time with us.
If this lesson helps you, give this video a big thumbs-up.
Click the subscribe button and the little bell, too.
That way you won't forget to join us for our next lesson.
You are all great students and we're proud of your effort.
Keep practicing. Remember, big change often starts with one small honest habit.
And a better year is built in normal days, not perfect days.
Exactly. Step by step, your choices shape your year.
So, keep learning, keep speaking, and keep moving forward.
Have a wonderful day, evening, and night.
Keep learning, keep speaking, and be kind to yourself.
Bye, everyone.
